sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page selu1243 (Selungai Murut) and semb1240 (Sembakung Murut)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: the sole reference for both languages is Spitzack 1984 (subclassification comments); Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Chapter 11 (Southwest Sabah), pp. 359-403.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Selungai stress. 'Murut Selungai' (MSel) appears in the abbreviation list and once in the discussion of the *ma- > *a- prefix shift in central/southern Murutic languages (p. 384); the chapter is historical subgrouping with no synchronic phonology or stress statement for any Murutic language. Its 13 'stress' hits all concern Philippine languages or Proto-Austronesian.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Southwest Sabah revisited. Oceanic Linguistics 52(1): 36-68.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lobel's published Southwest Sabah subgrouping paper draws on his own fieldwork wordlists including Murut Selungai; it is historical, but it is the only peer-reviewed work known to use first-hand Selungai data and may contain a transcription note on stress/accent. Low expectation given the dissertation chapter (same content) is silent.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene (compiler). 'Selungai Murut' in Numeral Systems of the World's Languages (MPI-EVA lingweb). Data supplied by David C. Moody, SIL International, Sabah, Malaysia, 6 November 1987, 'taken from SIL linguistic survey'. Two page variants (Indonesia-side and Sabah-side headers, identical data).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: ten numeral forms only (1 daono, 2 duwo, 3 talu, 4 apat, 5 limo, 6 onom, 7 toloʔ, 8 balɔ, 9 siam, 10 apulu), no stress or length marks, comment limited to 'decimal system'. Wordlist-only data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Spitzack, John A. 1984. The Murutic language family. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: A survey report, 155-223. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. Section 4.9 'Selungai Murut language', p. 208 (PDF p. 216).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Survey report only (lexicostatistics and intelligibility testing). The Selungai section gives location (six or seven villages on the Sapulut/Sembakung River), population 600-800 in Sabah, no ethnonym, closest lexically to Sembakung Murut. The whole 368-page volume has no hit for stress/accent/penult/suprasegmental; no phonology of any Murutic language is given (the literature section refers to Prentice 1971 for Murutic phonology).

sources.citation: Prentice, D.J. 1971. The Murut languages of Sabah. Pacific Linguistics C-18. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not a Selungai source: a Timugon Murut grammar with phonological/morphological outlines of other Sabah Murutic varieties (Prentice's data predate the identification of Selungai as a group). No mention of Selungai or Sembakung in the text layer; the text layer is poor (letter-spaced scanned) and I did not re-scanned it since it is out of scope. Kept only as the nearest related-language description.
